solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Engineer studies vehicle stopping short at road junction (9)

indicatorNotes.stopping short: the vehicle stops short of its full length, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: to con is to study closely
TRUCK without its last letter
a T-junction is shaped like the letter T

annotation.surface: An engineer poring over a vehicle that pulls up just short of a road junction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun but is the verb, to build. CON for study is old-fashioned but a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to engineer a bridge is to build it, the verb sense rather than the job title.

entries.clue: Old revue that’s had some rejigging works (6)

indicatorNotes.had some rejigging: rejigging rearranges, so the letters of REVUE are reordered

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
the letters of REVUE rearranged

annotation.surface: A tired old stage revue that has been reworked before it goes on again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb finishing the sentence; it is the noun, an artist's whole body of work.
annotation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is the complete works of an artist or writer.

entries.clue: Most discerning characters of this age stifled (6)

indicatorNotes.characters of: the answer is made of letters (characters) found in the following words

blocks.note: thiS AGE STifled

annotation.surface: A complaint that the wisest people of our era have been silenced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people, which fits 'most discerning'; here it means letters, and the answer runs across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Sagest is the superlative of sage, wise, so most discerning.

entries.clue: Come back about wrong requiring legal action? (6)

blocks.note: re = about, concerning
a tort is a civil wrong for which one can sue

annotation.surface: Someone returning to a grievance that might end up in court.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that TORT is defined by a description rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A retort is a comeback; to retort is to come back with a sharp reply.

entries.clue: Wild animal in vehicle I fight, squashing tail (7)

indicatorNotes.squashing tail: the tail of the word is squashed flat, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as printed
BOUT without its last letter

annotation.surface: A wild animal fighting inside a car and getting its tail squashed.
annotation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a wild animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Squashing' reads as the animal crushing its tail in the car; it tells you to cut the tail letter off BOUT.

entries.clue: Chemical compound in body that could make one inert soon (9)

indicatorNotes.could make one: the letters could be made into one new word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A body chemical that might soon leave a person sluggish.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly true to life: serotonin is linked with mood and sleep, so it could indeed make one inert.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: serotonin is a neurotransmitter the body makes, tied to mood and sleep.

entries.clue: A sermon about God’s ultimate loving (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimate: ultimate means last, so the last letter of God's
indicatorNotes.about: the sermon goes about, around, the D

blocks.note: taken as printed
last letter of GOD
an oration is a formal speech

annotation.surface: A preacher's sermon on the love of God.
annotation.walkthrough: A-ORATION wraps around the D, so the D sits just after the opening A.
annotation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love, so loving as a noun.
annotation.definitionNote: loving here is the noun (the act of loving), matching ADORATION

entries.clue: Ruining brill experience in restaurant? (9)

blocks.note: brill and def are both slang for excellent
what you do at a restaurant

annotation.surface: A disappointing meal of brill, the flatfish, ruining a night out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brill' looks like the fish on a restaurant menu; it is British slang for brilliant, as is 'def'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of thwarting: a defeating blow is one that wrecks a plan or hope.

entries.clue: Tinker needs a bit of metal as you might say? (6)

indicatorNotes.as you might say: points to how the word is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: a medal is a piece of metal

annotation.surface: A tinker, the travelling mender, needing a scrap of metal for a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' reads as the pot-mender, a noun; it is the verb, to fiddle with.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to tinker is to fiddle with things you should leave alone, which is to interfere.

entries.clue: Move, then wait — not right in terms of financial planning? (9)

indicatorNotes.not right: remove R, the abbreviation for right

blocks.note: to budge is to move slightly
TARRY, to wait, with one R removed

annotation.surface: Hesitant advice to make a move, then hold back, about how to handle money.
annotation.walkthrough: BUDGE itself hints at the answer's root, budget.
annotation.definitionFit: Budgetary means relating to a budget, a financial plan.

entries.clue: Having a frog or some other animal, we hear? (6)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is sound, so the word is chosen by how it is pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: a horse is another animal

annotation.surface: A question about owning a frog or some other pet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having a frog' is the idiom 'a frog in one's throat', a croaky voice, not a pet.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'a frog in the throat' is a croak in the voice, so having one leaves you rough-voiced.

entries.clue: Denounce writing that includes plagiarism (9)

indicatorNotes.that includes: the first word takes the second inside it

blocks.note: prose is ordinary writing
a crib is something copied

annotation.surface: Condemning a piece of work that has been copied from somewhere else.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to proscribe something is to condemn it publicly and ban it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plagiarism' reads as the charge being denounced; here it is schoolroom slang for copied work, the thing a cheat copies from.

entries.clue: Bird — over time cat will get it (6)

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as printed

annotation.surface: A warning that, given time, the cat will catch the bird.
annotation.walkthrough: TOM is followed by T and IT; the surface's grim prediction is the order the pieces are laid down.
annotation.definitionFit: The tomtit is a small bird, usually the blue tit.

entries.clue: Player in pantos — Mrs looking silly (9)

indicatorNotes.looking silly: the letters are in a silly, disordered state

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: An actor in a pantomime, the British Christmas stage show, next to a dame looking ridiculous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Player' fits the theatre picture; it means a sportsman. A panto is a British family Christmas show full of silly costumes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a player of a sport, as opposed to an actor on stage.

entries.clue: Put a stop to female rot with rebuke (9)

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
rust is rot in metal
to rate is an old word for to scold

annotation.surface: A woman ending some nonsense with a sharp telling-off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rot' reads as nonsense; it is decay, RUST. RATE for scold is archaic but common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: frustrating a scheme thwarts it, halting it before it succeeds.

entries.clue: Variable disciple, a beast inside (9)

indicatorNotes.inside: the second part goes inside the first

blocks.note: Peter was one of Jesus's disciples
A + RAM, a male sheep

annotation.surface: A fickle follower who turns out to have an animal lurking within.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Variable' reads as an adjective describing the disciple; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: In maths and programming a parameter is a variable quantity.

entries.clue: Reggae with a measure of loudness outside uni (3)

indicatorNotes.outside: the first part goes around the second

blocks.note: dB is the symbol for decibel
U is the abbreviation for university

annotation.surface: Reggae played loud enough to be heard outside the university.
annotation.definitionFit: Dub is a style of reggae built on remixed instrumental tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: dB is the decibel, the unit of loudness; it wraps around U, the usual crossword letter for university.

entries.clue: Private office in garden lacking roof (3)

indicatorNotes.lacking roof: in a down answer the roof is the top, the start of the word, which is removed

blocks.note: GARDEN with its top letters, GAR, taken off

annotation.surface: A home office set up in a garden shed that has lost its roof.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is also sitting at the end of 'garden', which helps confirm it.
annotation.definitionFit: A den is a private room for work or retreat.

entries.clue: Only a clumsy boat will capsize (3)

indicatorNotes.will capsize: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down answer the word is turned over

blocks.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

annotation.surface: A warning that only an unwieldy boat will overturn.
annotation.definitionFit: But can mean only, as in 'nothing but'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tub' is a disparaging word for a slow, broad boat. 'Only' looks like an adverb for the whole sentence; it is the definition.

entries.clue: One material or another put around fancy lace (7)

indicatorNotes.put around: turned around, so the word is reversed
indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy suggests something elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rep is another fabric, a ribbed cloth
the letters of LACE rearranged

annotation.surface: Choosing between fabrics, with fancy lace wrapped around one of them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One material or another' reads as a single phrase; it splits into the definition and 'another', a second fabric, REP.
annotation.definitionFit: Percale is a closely woven cotton fabric, one material.

entries.clue: Marriage loses love with invasion of my fantasy creature! (7)

indicatorNotes.loses: the letter for love is taken away
indicatorNotes.with invasion of: the second part invades, goes inside, the first

blocks.note: UNION without O, love (zero in tennis)
cor! is a British exclamation like 'my!'

annotation.surface: A marriage losing its love after a mythical beast barges in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive; it is an exclamation of surprise, and COR is its British slang equivalent.
annotation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a mythical horned horse, a fantasy creature.

entries.clue: Fool, a single person losing head (3)

blocks.note: UNIT, a single entity, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A lonely fool who has lost his head.
annotation.walkthrough: NIT is short for nitwit, a mild British insult.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: nit, short for nitwit, is a mild word for a silly person.

entries.clue: Always remembered for time-wasting? Very bad (7)

indicatorNotes.for time-wasting: the T for time is wasted, removed

blocks.note: IMMORTAL without T

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether wasting time is really so wicked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time-wasting' reads as idleness; split it and the T for time is what goes to waste.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, stretched: immoral means morally wrong, and 'very bad' is the loose everyday sense.

entries.clue: Heathen god with inadequate set of values, not one to be admired (6)

indicatorNotes.inadequate: falling short, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
SCALE, a set of values, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A pagan deity with poor morals who deserves no respect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set of values' reads as morals; it is a scale of numbers, which then falls short by a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: a rascal is a rogue, a person of bad character nobody looks up to.

entries.clue: Nervous, a certain broadcasting boss before committee finally (2,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'committee', its last letter, is used

blocks.note: as in 'a certain person' = 'one person'
Director-General, the head of the BBC
last letter of COMMITTEE

annotation.surface: A BBC chief anxious before facing a committee.
annotation.walkthrough: The DG, Director-General, runs the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be on edge is to be tense and jumpy.

entries.clue: Blast on the horn when releasing a religious work (6)

indicatorNotes.when releasing: to release something is to let it go, so the A is let go from the word

blocks.clueFragment: Blast on the horn when releasing a
blocks.note: TANTARA, a fanfare, without one A

annotation.surface: A fanfare sounded at the launch of a sacred text.
annotation.walkthrough: Tantara is an old word for a trumpet flourish.
annotation.definitionFit: A tantra is a Hindu or Buddhist sacred text.

entries.clue: Like seaweed, cold — around zero (6)

indicatorNotes.around: the first word goes around the letter

blocks.note: algid is a rare word for cold
O looks like zero

annotation.surface: A description of seaweed as cold, near freezing.
annotation.definitionFit: Algoid means like algae, such as seaweed.
annotation.walkthrough: The word for cold is rare, from Latin algidus; 'like seaweed' fits because seaweeds are algae.

entries.clue: Bad men drunk with ale not beyond redemption (9)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk is disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters

annotation.surface: Wrongdoers drunk on beer who might still be reformed.
annotation.definitionFit: Something amendable can be put right, so is not beyond redemption.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' sits between 'Bad men' and 'ale' as if describing them; it is the instruction to mix up all their letters.

entries.clue: Possible course fixed around globe (6)

indicatorNotes.around: the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: set = fixed
an orb is a globe

annotation.surface: A route decided on around the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a route around the globe; it is a course in a meal, and 'possible' marks the definition as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a sorbet is served as one course of a meal, often between the main dishes, hence 'possible'.

entries.clue: Knowledge of game conveyed in publication (9)

blocks.note: an edition is a publication
RU is rugby union

annotation.surface: Expertise about a sport passed on through a book.
annotation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union, a sport widely played in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: erudition is deep learning, the knowledge gained from much reading.

entries.clue: Insect has got the lady’s plant? Only a bit of it (6)

annotation.definition: plant? Only a bit of it

blocks.note: an ant is an insect
her = belonging to the lady

annotation.surface: An insect has taken a woman's houseplant, or at least a nibble of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is spread out: the answer is not a plant but only part of one.
annotation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing part of a flower's stamen.

entries.clue: In Salvador see mum dance (9)

indicatorNotes.In: the second part goes in the first

blocks.note: Salvador Allende, president of Chile 1970 to 1973
ma = mum

annotation.surface: A trip to El Salvador to watch mother dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salvador' looks like the country El Salvador; it is the first name of Chile's president Allende, which stands for his surname.
annotation.definitionFit: The allemande is a stately German court dance.
